about.title: About Me
bio: My name is Arturo, although many know me as [[R2]]. I studied TSAFAD, but after several years dedicating myself to it, I decided to make a shift towards the tech sector —another of my great passions— driven by my interest in creating, building, and solving.

I've been in contact with computers since I was little, although it wasn't until 2022 that I started to delve into the world of programming. In January 2025, I made the decision to train seriously and in a structured way. Since then, I've developed multiple projects and have many more in mind that I'd like to carry out and monetize.
I consider myself a [[self-taught]] person; learning on my own has been a constant in my life and that has made me resourceful, independent, and always in search of new solutions.

description: Internship at NTT DATA within the Java and Spring Boot training program. We worked on backend with Spring Boot (REST services), testing with JUnit and Mockito, PostgreSQL, frontend with Angular, and an integrative project where we applied everything we learned.

The final project was developed as a team using Git and GitHub to coordinate work: each feature in its own branch, changes integrated through Pull Requests and reviewed before merging. A real-world approach to team collaboration with version control.
We also completed specialized courses in prompt engineering with generative AI and unit testing with mocks, complementing the technical training with skills in two key areas of modern development.
achievements: Git and GitHub as a coordination tool: applied Git to manage teamwork with feature branches, atomic commits, Pull Requests, and controlled merges. I already knew Git — here we implemented it as a real team coordination tool.

Backend development with mini projects: built several small Java Spring Boot projects implementing REST endpoints, services, and business logic. Each mini project covered a different technology or concept, allowing me to learn Spring Boot progressively and hands-on.

Advanced SQL in PostgreSQL: worked with complex queries including nested subqueries, views, stored procedures, functions, and triggers. Learned to design and optimize database schemas beyond basic CRUD operations.

Angular course with standalone components and Signals: completed a dedicated Angular course covering the new standalone component architecture, Signals for reactivity, and ecosystem best practices. Built a complete frontend applying these concepts.

Unit testing with mocks course: specialized training in creating mocks and verifying behavior with Mockito and JUnit. Learned to isolate dependencies in unit tests, simulate behaviors, and precisely verify object interactions.

Prompt engineering with generative AI course: structured training in advanced prompt design — closed vs. open prompts, zero-shot and few-shot prompting, chain-of-thought for step-by-step reasoning. Hyperparameter configuration (temperature, Top P, stop sequences) to regulate model creativity. Precise SQL query generation with explicit constraints, architectural platform comparison (ChatGPT vs. Perplexity), iterative data refinement workflows, and fundamentals of MLOps and legal security in model deployment.

Agile methodologies in practice: the team worked with bi-weekly sprints and daily standups. Learned to estimate tasks, communicate blockers on time, and use the Kanban board to prioritize pending work.

Technical documentation: wrote technical documentation for the features I implemented, including design decisions, available endpoints, and usage examples. This taught me the importance of keeping documentation alive and accessible to the team.

v12-ui.shortDescription: React component library and hooks. Tailwind CSS v4, full TypeScript typing, tree-shakeable.
description: 10 components (Button, Stack, Text, AnimatedBackground, MagicText, MagicLogo, MagicMouseFollower, Accordion, Select, Toggle) + 2 hooks (useDataTheme, useReducedMotion).
Polymorphic components, automatic dark mode, canvas particle effects, WAI-ARIA accessibility, CSS variables theming, and zero-config setup.

details.title: 10 Components + 2 Hooks
details.text: Button, Stack, Text, AnimatedBackground, MagicText, MagicLogo, MagicMouseFollower, Accordion, Select, Toggle. Plus useDataTheme and useReducedMotion hooks. Full TypeScript with autocomplete and strict types.

details.title: Tree-shakeable & Zero-config
details.text: Built with Vite, exports both ESM and CJS modules. Tree-shaking ensures only the components you import end up in production. No plugins or providers needed. On npm with full Storybook docs.

details.title: Polymorphic Components
details.text: Button renders as <button> or <a>. Text and Stack render as any HTML tag. Full polymorphic refs and type safety. Automatic dark mode reads data-theme on <html> or falls back to prefers-color-scheme.

details.title: Canvas Particle Effects
details.text: MagicText assembles text from particles. MagicLogo disassembles images into particles. MagicMouseFollower creates particle trails. All use spring physics and respect prefers-reduced-motion.

details.title: WAI-ARIA Accessibility
details.text: Accordion: WAI-ARIA accordion pattern with arrow-key navigation (up/down/home/end). Select: WAI-ARIA combobox with keyboard nav and dropdown animation. Toggle: WAI-ARIA switch pattern.

details.title: Themeable via CSS Variables
details.text: Customize colors using CSS variables in your stylesheet. Semantic tokens map to Tailwind utilities. Works with Tailwind CSS v4 @theme directive. Import the stylesheet and use components directly.

english-web.shortDescription: Full-stack educational platform. Vanilla frontend, Node.js backend, Turso + Prisma, Redis sessions, JWT auth, and hexagonal architecture.
description: Why this project? Because I wanted to truly understand how a web application works. Not 'learn React' or 'set up Next.js'. Understand the fundamentals: HTTP, authentication, databases, server-side vs client-side rendering, session management, and above all, architecture.
The decision was deliberate: zero frontend frameworks, zero magic dependencies. Everything here, I understand and control. Built to learn — not to impress with framework names.

details.title: Architecture > Framework
details.text: Backend structured with Hexagonal / Screaming Architecture. The src/ folder screams what it does: auth/, user/, shared/. No matter what framework or database I use — the core business logic is isolated. If I change Prisma for Drizzle or Turso for PostgreSQL tomorrow, I only touch infrastructure/.
details.code:
src/
  auth/
    application/ → use-cases
    domain/       → entities, ports
    infrastructure/ → adapters (Prisma, Redis, JWT)

details.title: Authentication from Scratch
details.text: No NextAuth, Lucia, or magic. Complete implementation: email/password with bcrypt, Google OAuth 2.0 with full verification flow, dual JWT (access 15min + refresh 7d with rotation), Redis for active refresh tokens with TTL, secure cookies (httpOnly, sameSite, secure). Can close sessions actively — revoke tokens. Something JWT alone can't do.

details.title: Vanilla Frontend, Real HTTP
details.text: Traditional HTML pages (index.html, lessons.html, user_profile.html). No React, no Vue, no router. Every navigation is a real HTTP request. The problem: full page reloads. The solution: don't force SPA — accept traditional navigation and optimize what matters: cached stylesheets, deferred scripts, and async session verification via fetch('/auth/me').

details.title: CSS 3D Flip Cards
details.text: Vocabulary and lesson cards use a 3D flip effect with pure CSS. Zero JavaScript for the animation. The GPU renders the 3D via transform-style: preserve-3d and backface-visibility: hidden. Only a class toggle drives the animation.

details.title: JSON-driven Content
details.text: Game and lesson content is defined in JSON files. Each level is an object with words, translations, visual hints, and difficulty config. Adding a new level means creating a new JSON file. No HTML, no CSS, no engine changes. Loading a new level is fetch('/niveles/nuevo.json'). Anyone who can write JSON can extend the project.

details.title: What I Learned (that doesn't show in code)
details.text: Architecture > Framework — good structure survives any tech change. JWT is not 'state in client' — it's a token you validate, rotate, and revoke. You can't truly log out without Redis or similar. CSS 3D is not 'animation' — it's perspective and how the GPU renders layers. Not every project needs to be SPA. JSON as a content format decouples data from presentation cleanly.
